annotations.text:
Table Cvt D · axis: column cards.
Why: Mobile is one card per species (Congo, then Timneh) listing all 12 traits as label: value pairs, so a buyer reads one bird top to bottom the way the live for-sale pages present a single bird. Tablet puts the two cards side by side; Desktop is a classic 4-column table with the Timneh column tinted rgba(45,106,79,.08) because the three decided Edge rows in the round-1 copy (Price, Maturity, Temperament) all go to Timneh, and a 16px check marks each of those rows. Measured Mobile root 1582px (round-1 A was 3,398px, B 1,661px), Tablet 935px, Desktop 980px. Probe: 0 overflow, 0 hit targets under 44, 0 contrast fails, min Mobile text 14px.
Trade-off: on Mobile the Congo value for a trait is a full card-scroll away from the Timneh value, so row-by-row comparison is the weakest of the three; the Edge chips live only in the Timneh card.

Table Cvt E · axis: banded rows.
Why: each trait is a full-width warm band (#f6efe8, uppercase) carrying the Edge verdict at its right end, with the Congo and Timneh values in a 2-up grid under it at every width, so the two values sit next to each other on a phone without any toggle, tab or script. Desktop keeps the identical bands inside a 1px-bordered 18px-radius container at max-width 960 centered, so the same DOM serves all three viewports. Measured Mobile root 1556px, Tablet 1405px, Desktop 1450px. Probe: 0 overflow, 0 contrast fails, min Mobile text 14px.
Trade-off: it is the tallest of the three at Desktop (1450px versus 980px for D and 873px for F) because every trait spends a band plus a value row, and the Desktop 960 container leaves the 1120 content width partly unused.

(Recommended) Table Cvt F · axis: accordion rows.
Why: Mobile is twelve native <details> rows, each summary 48px tall showing the trait name and the leading species (a green check plus Timneh on the three decided rows, Compare on the nine even ones), expanding to both values and the Edge line; the first row ships open. It is the shortest Mobile answer measured this round at 1056px, against 1582px for D, 1556px for E and 3,398px for round-1 A, so the whole comparison fits in roughly two phone screens and the verdict for every trait is visible before a single tap. Desktop and Tablet are a hairline table with no vertical rules, 1px row rules and a 16px inline SVG check in the leading cell, 873px at 1440, the lightest of the three. Zero JavaScript: <details> is native. Probe: 0 overflow, 0 hit targets under 44, 0 contrast fails.
Trade-off: the values themselves are hidden until a tap on Mobile, so a buyer who wants the numbers rather than the verdict taps up to twelve times; the collapsed default also keeps that text out of the first paint for crawlers that do not expand details.

Table Mvf D · axis: column cards.
Why: same construction as Cvt D so the two tables read as one system: Mobile one card per sex (Male, Female) with the three buyer questions as label: value pairs plus a separate Telling them apart card carrying the DNA-sexing fact verbatim; Tablet 2-up; Desktop a 3-column classic table with the fact as a colspan row. No column is tinted: the round-1 copy names no winner in any of the three rows, so there is no C.A.Gs pick to shade, and shading one would invent a verdict. Measured Mobile root 907px, Tablet 594px, Desktop 500px. Probe clean.
Trade-off: with only three traits the two Mobile cards are mostly header and padding, and the male value for a question sits a card-scroll away from the female value.

(Recommended) Table Mvf E · axis: banded rows.
Why: the three buyer questions are long-sentence answers (the longest cell is 71 characters), which is exactly the content that broke the live table at 375 in round 1 (one or two words per line). A full-width question band with the Male and Female answers in a 2-up grid under it gives each answer half the width at every viewport with the two answers adjacent, and the Telling them apart fact becomes a fourth band with a full-width paragraph, so nothing is hidden and nothing scrolls sideways. Measured Mobile root 765px, Tablet 598px, Desktop 598px in the 960 container. Probe: 0 overflow, 0 contrast fails, min Mobile text 14px.
Trade-off: it is taller than F on Mobile (765px versus 459px) because every answer is shown at once, and half-width columns at 390 wrap the longer answers to three lines.

Table Mvf F · axis: accordion rows.
Why: Mobile is four native <details> rows (three questions plus the fact), 48px summaries, the first open; because no row has a winner every summary reads Compare, and the fact row reads Fact. It is the shortest Mvf Mobile board at 459px (D 907px, E 765px). Desktop and Tablet are the hairline table with no vertical rules and 1px row rules; there is no leading cell and therefore no check mark anywhere, which the note says so nobody reads its absence as a missing asset. Probe clean.
Trade-off: with no verdicts to preview, the collapsed summaries carry almost no information (a name and the word Compare), so the buyer must open all four rows to learn anything; the accordion pays its cost without earning it here.
